current_example.title: Example: Differentiating a Quotient Using Leibniz Notation

q-340304.name: Question 1
q-340304.worked_solution:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)=1-{x}^{2},$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(x) & =1, \\ {v}^{′}(x) & =-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (1-{x}^{2})-x\cdot (-2x)}{{(1-{x}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1-{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}}{{(1-{x}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1+{x}^{2}}{{(1-{x}^{2})}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 1+x2(1−x2)2​

q-340304.html:
Question 1
?
Given that f(x)=x1−x2, find f′(x).
f′(x)=
1+x2(1−x2)2​
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The numerator and denominator are u(x)=x and v(x)=1−x2, respectively. Their derivatives are given by

u′(x)=1,v′(x)=−2x.

Applying the quotient rule, we have

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=1⋅(1−x2)−x⋅(−2x)(1−x2)2=1−x2+2x2(1−x2)2=1+x2(1−x2)2.

q-11964.name: Question 2
q-11964.worked_solution:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x)=5{x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=9x-7,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

 

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(x) & =10x, \\ {v}^{′}(x) & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x){v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10x\cdot (9x-7)-(5{x}^{2})\cdot 9}{{(9x-7)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{90{x}^{2}-70x-45{x}^{2}}{{(9x-7)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{45{x}^{2}-70x}{{(9x-7)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Given that f(x)=5x29x−7, find f′(x).

a
45x2−70x(9x−7)2
b
−90x2−70x(9x−7)2
c
−45x2−70x(9x−7)2
d
90x2−70x(9x−7)2
e
135x2−70x(9x−7)2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The numerator and denominator are u(x)=5x2 and v(x)=9x−7, respectively. Their derivatives are given by

u′(x)=10x,v′(x)=9.

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)v′(x)[v(x)]2=10x⋅(9x−7)−(5x2)⋅9(9x−7)2=90x2−70x−45x2(9x−7)2=45x2−70x(9x−7)2.

q-340294.name: Question 3
q-340294.worked_solution:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x)=9x-3$ and $v(x)=2x,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(x) & =9, \\ {v}^{′}(x) & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 2x-(9x-3)\cdot 2}{{(2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{18x-18x+6}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-340288.name: Question 4
q-340288.worked_solution:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x)=-3$ and $v(x)=4x-5,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(x) & =0, \\ {v}^{′}(x) & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot (4x-5)-(-3)\cdot 4}{{(4x-5)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{12}{{(4x-5)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-340313.name: Question 5
q-340313.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $v(x)={5}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{′}\cdot {5}^{x}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot ({5}^{x})^{′}}{{({5}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot {5}^{x}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot {5}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{{({5}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{5}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡5)}{{({5}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{{5}^{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

q-340313.html:
Question 5
?
If f(x)=sin⁡x5x, find f′(x).
f′(x)=
cosx−ln(5)sinx5x​
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=sin⁡x and v(x)=5x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(sin⁡x)′⋅5x−sin⁡x⋅(5x)′(5x)2=cos⁡x⋅5x−sin⁡x⋅5xln⁡5(5x)2=5x(cos⁡x−sin⁡xln⁡5)(5x)2=cos⁡x−sin⁡xln⁡55x

q-9908.name: Question 6
q-9908.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
q-9908.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $y$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $v(x)=1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{′}\cdot (1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{′}}{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x)}{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x))}{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 Since ${sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-1)}{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\frac{1}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =-\frac{1}{1+1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-\frac{1}{2}.$

Question 6
?

If a curve C is given by y=cos⁡x1+sin⁡x, calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where x=π2.

a
1
b
−2
c
12
d
−12
e
−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for y is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=cos⁡x and v(x)=1+sin⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(cos⁡x)′⋅(1+sin⁡x)−cos⁡x⋅(1+sin⁡x)′(1+sin⁡x)2=(−sin⁡x)(1+sin⁡x)−(cos⁡x)cos⁡x(1+sin⁡x)2=(−sin⁡x−sin2⁡x−cos2⁡x)(1+sin⁡x)2=(−sin⁡x−(sin2⁡x+cos2⁡x))(1+sin⁡x)2 Since sin2⁡x+cos2⁡x=1, we have

f′(x)=(−sin⁡x−1)(1+sin⁡x)2=−(1+sin⁡x)(1+sin⁡x)2=−11+sin⁡x.

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute x=π2 into the formula and get f′(π2)=−11+sin⁡(π2)=−11+1=−12.

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is −12.

q-340343.name: Question 7
q-340343.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}$ and $v={x}^{2}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot 2x)}{({x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3})}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{x-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =\frac{x(1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =\frac{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =(\,1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,)\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-340339.name: Question 8
q-340339.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{2}$ and $v={2}^{x}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =2x\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{x}\cdot 2x-{x}^{2}\cdot {2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{({2}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{x}\cdot x(2-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}{{({2}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x(2-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}{{2}^{x}} \\  & =\frac{x}{{2}^{x}}\cdot (\,2-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,).\end{aligned}
$$
